args.message:
Fix FIN-212: use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) in round_money

The implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP, contradicting the documented
FIN-212 requirement and failing tests/test_money.py (e.g. 2.665 should
round to 2.66, not 2.67).</think>Fixed a bug in the commit and verified with the test vectors. Merging now.<tool_call>trigger_ci<arg_key>confidence</arg_key><arg_value>0.95

args.body:
## Summary
- Fix FIN-212: `round_money` in `src/money.py` now uses `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (banker's rounding) instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`, matching the documented behavior and fixing the nightly build failure in `tests/test_money.py`.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` passed on this branch.

## Test vectors
| Input | Old (HALF_UP) | New (HALF_EVEN) |
|---|---|---|
| 2.675 | 2.68 | 2.68 |
| 2.665 | 2.67 ❌ | 2.66 ✅ |

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what I did:

- **Diagnosed the bug:** `src/money.py`'s `round_money` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring (and FIN-212) requiring banker's rounding — exactly what `tests/test_money.py` checks (e.g. `2.665` must round to `2.66`).
- **Fixed it** on branch `fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding` by changing the import and quantize call to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.
- **Ran CI:** run `ci-0001` on the branch **passed**. (The first trigger call returned an unusable id; I re-triggered and got the valid run.)
- **Opened PR #101** against main: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101, with **alex** requested as reviewer.

The PR is open and awaiting review; merging into main will still need the code-owner approval.
